title: Independent reading: Galatians 2:15–21
subtitle: Read justification language through clauses and contrast.
overview: Galatians 2:15–21 is a tightly argued passage with key prepositions, genitives, participles, and contrasts. Map its claims rather than starting with its debated terms.
Watch how negative statements, διὰ phrases, and the first-person singular conclusion develop the argument.

items.grc: οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
items.en: A person is not justified by works of law except through faith of/in Jesus Christ.

items.grc: ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός.
items.en: And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.
